newsitem.title: USA: Dick Morris says he's getting treatment he deserves.
newsitem.headline: Dick Morris says he's getting treatment he deserves.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's former chief strategist Dick Morris, who resigned in disgrace in August, describes himself as weak and obsessive and says most people these days are "treating me as unkindly as I deserve."

In one of the few interviews he has given since resigning after it was revealed he had an affair with a prostitute, the only thing Morris seemed proud of was the political stategy he and Clinton designed for the re-election campaign.

He said repositioning the president as a centrist -- rather than a liberal -- has held up, and he predicted Clinton would win re-election in a landslide with the Democrats recapturing both houses of Congress.
"Bob Dole will win fewer than 10 states and win less than 100 electoral votes. The Democrats will wind up with 52 or 53 seats in the Senate and a majority of about 30 in the House."

Morris resigned as Clinton's political strategist on the day the president made his acceptance speech at the Democratic National Convention. The resignation was forced by revelations he had a year-long affair with a $200-an-hour call girl, who sold her story to a supermarket tabloid.

"I have been recovering from the scandal and my rapid fall from grace and trying to put my marriage together and make clear to my wife and anyone who listens that I feel badly and deeply ashamed," Morris said in a telephone interview with Reuters on Thursday.
"It is a long process and I can't possibly predict how it will come out. I promised (my wife) that I will do it in private. Most people are treating me as unkindly as I deserve," he said.

"My career is not the No. 1 thing on my mind. The main thing is to overcome the weaknesses and obsessions that led me to self-destruct. I also want to preserve the centre of my life, which is my marriage."

Asked what caused his fall, Morris said, "I think the unique environment that I was in, in Washington, tested my character and my maturity and it was found wanting, like a bridge that you don't know is weak until a storm hits."
He declined comment on whether he and Clinton still keep in touch or whether he talks to the many prominent Republicans he had advised, including Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott.
